overview: 2...e6 is a gateway rather than a set-up: after 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Black chooses the Taimanov (...Nc6), the Kan (...a6) or the Scheveningen (...d6, ...Nf6), with 3.Nc3 giving the Paulsen/Kan/Taimanov move orders. Black opens the diagonal for the f8-bishop and prepares ...d5 or ...Nc6/...a6 in a flexible way, with a solid ...e6/...d6 pawn chain and queenside counterplay. The name 'French' is only a naming convention: the pawn structure is Sicilian, not a French one. White's main choice is 3.d4 (about 61% of moves at 2500); rarer third moves are 3.d3, 3.g3, 3.c3 and Westerinen's 3.b3 (Bb2, occasional in the 1970s). At higher levels play is heavily theoretical.

white_ideas.idea: 3.d4 and the Open Sicilian: establish a classical centre, then choose Maroczy-bind or Nb5 ideas depending on Black's set-up
3.Nc3 (Paulsen move order) keeping options of d4 later; transposes to Taimanov or Kan
Quiet alternatives: 3.d3, 3.g3, 3.b3 (Westerinen, Bb2) to avoid Open Sicilian theory

black_ideas.idea: Open the f8-bishop's diagonal and prepare ...Nc6 (Taimanov) or ...a6 (Kan) while keeping ...d5 and ...d6 flexible
Kan 4...a6 avoids the early Nb5 pressure of the Taimanov and gives manoeuvres such as ...Nd7-c5
...d5 break prepared by ...e6, with recapture options, to liberate Black's position

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian with ...e6 and ...d6/...d7: solid chain, Black has good dark squares while White controls light squares and the centre, sometimes a Maroczy bind
Paulsen/Kan: pawns on c-file exchanged, half-open c-file for Black, small pawn centre

character.notes: s1 rates it Sharp and reports about 80% of moves at higher levels are known theory, meaning forcing, well-mapped positions. s2 describes the French Variation as a more flexible set-up that usually avoids the more tactical lines. These conflict somewhat: the move itself is flexible and solid-looking, but the lines after 3.d4 (Taimanov, Kan, Scheveningen) are theory-heavy with real attacking chances for White. Typical play depends on the move order White picks.

gambit.notes: No material is given in the main lines.

soundness.notes: Sound and balanced: s1 gives White 46.8%, Black 48.7%, draws 4.5% over 51 million games. Black scores slightly better than White at this level of aggregate. Nothing calls it dubious.

structure.notes: After 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 the d-pawns are traded and the centre becomes semi-open: White has e4, Black has a half-open c-file. Rarer 3.d3/3.g3/3.b3 keep the centre closed or in tension.

approach.notes: A flexible set of pawn moves (...c5, ...e6) that can be played against 1.e4 with several piece set-ups. Not a system that ignores White's reply, since Black's piece placement depends on White's third move. Moderately popular at strong level: s1 reports 1.03% of games at 2500 in 2025 (peak 1.28% in 2015); Pia Cramling (351 games as Black) and Gyula Sax (134 as White) are named practitioners. The Taimanov and Kan are main-line choices of strong players.

level.notes: Judged for Black. Move-order flexibility with ...e6 is friendly because Black can postpone commitment, and the Taimanov/Kan plans are clear (s3: understand ideas and plans over names). But s1 notes about 80% of moves are theory at higher levels and the Open Sicilian after 3.d4 is a deep theory area, and s2 notes the Sicilian carries a lot of theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Taimanov
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nc6
sublines_that_differ.how: Piece-play with ...Nc6, ...Qc7, ...a6; considered the most comfortable e6 Sicilian for Black (snippet).

sublines_that_differ.name: Kan
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 a6
sublines_that_differ.how: Flexible, avoids Nb5; compact structure with ...Nd7-c5 ideas.

sublines_that_differ.name: Scheveningen / Open (...d6)
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharper small-centre structure with attacking Keres-type options for White (own understanding, not sourced).

sublines_that_differ.name: Westerinen Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: Rare independent try with Bb2; quiet, avoids theory.

description.claim: The Sicilian French Variation is a highly flexible and resilient response to 1.e4
description.note: s2 calls the French Variation a more flexible set-up; s1 notes the transposition flexibility into Taimanov, Kan and Scheveningen.

description.claim: It blends the counter-attacking spirit of the Sicilian with the structural solidity of the French Defense
description.note: 'French' is a naming convention for 2...e6; the position has a Sicilian pawn structure, not a French one. The main lines after 3.d4 cxd4 are Taimanov, Kan and Scheveningen (s1), which are theory-heavy and rated Sharp, not 'French solidity'.

description.claim: Black aims to control the d5-square and launch a counter-thrust after completing development
description.note: ...e6 prepares the ...d5 break with recapture options (s1).

description.claim: Perfect for versatile players adept at both positional manoeuvring and sharp tactics
description.note: Opinion; no source frames it this way.

common_plans.claim: Black: prepare and execute the ...d5 pawn break to challenge White and liberate the position
Black: queenside counterplay with ...a6, ...b5 and ...Rc8, creating pressure against the e4-pawn
common_plans.note: ...a6 and queenside play fit the Kan (s3). ...Rc8 pressure on e4 specifically was not found.

common_plans.claim: White: use the central space advantage to develop an attack, often on the kingside, while restraining Black's counterplay
common_plans.note: s3 notes White controls light squares and the centre with Maroczy-bind possibilities; kingside attack was not specifically found.

common_plans.claim: White: control d5 and target a backward d6-pawn if it appears
common_plans.note: d5/d6 themes are real in Sveshnikov-type Sicilians, but not found as a stated plan for the e6 lines.
